items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The change is two lines and matches the reference exactly: a short comment `# Ensure base table is in aliases.` followed by a call to an existing method with a clear name. Formatting is consistent with the surrounding code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing helper `query.get_initial_alias()` inside `single_alias`. Collector and QuerySet.delete are untouched, there is no backend-specific branch, and no dead code or debug output was left behind.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: A minimal fix to an internal method that adds no error-handling paths and no magic constants. The delete/delete_regress/queries suites pass (456 tests), and so do the hidden tests (F2P 1/1, P2P 52/52).

items.name: Subquery dropped only for genuine single-table deletes
items.name_zh: 仅在真正单表删除时去掉子查询
items.evidence: The root cause is fixed in `single_alias` by registering the base alias before counting. Joined deletes still count more than one alias, so they keep the pk__in subquery. The MySQL compiler, which also relies on `single_alias`, benefits from the same fix. There is no special case for `.all()`.
